questions.question: A bar model is described in words: one long bar stands for a town's population of 8 000 people, and it is cut into 100 equal parts, so each part is 80 people. The population then grows by 2.5%, drawn as 2 extra parts plus half of another part added to the end of the bar. What is the new population?
questions.explain: Each part is 80 people, so 2.5 parts is 2.5 × 80 = 200 people of growth, and the new amount is 8 000 + 200 = 8 200 (same as 8 000 × 1.025). The usual trap is stopping at 200, which is only the extra piece, not the whole new bar.

questions.question: A bar model is described in words: a bar stands for 60 minutes of guitar practice and is cut into 4 equal parts of 15 minutes each. Practice time then increases by 175%, drawn as 7 more parts of 15 minutes joined onto the end of the original bar. How long is the new practice time?
questions.explain: The 7 extra parts are 7 × 15 = 105 minutes of increase, so the new bar is 60 + 105 = 165 minutes (same as 60 × 2.75). A percent over 100 does not mean you throw away the original bar, and it is not 0.175 — 175% as a decimal is 1.75.

questions.question: A bar model is described in words: a bar stands for the $2 000 in a soccer club's account and is cut into 100 equal parts worth $20 each. The account then falls by 0.5%, drawn as half of one part being erased from the end of the bar. How much money is in the account now?
questions.explain: Half of a $20 part is $10 taken away, so the account holds 2 000 − 10 = $1 990 (same as 2 000 × 0.995). Watch the decimal: 0.5% is 0.005, not 0.05 or 0.5, and the question asks what is left, not what was removed.

questions.question: A bar model is described in words: a bar stands for the 1 200 cans a class collected last year, cut into 100 equal parts of 12 cans each. This year the total drops by 0.25%, drawn as one quarter of a single part being crossed off. How many cans were collected this year?
questions.explain: A quarter of a 12-can part is 3 cans removed, so this year's total is 1 200 − 3 = 1 197 cans (same as 1 200 × 0.9975). The 3 cans is only the piece crossed off, and 0.25% is 0.0025 — not 0.025 or 0.25.

questions.question: Which calculation gives the new amount when 24 000 is increased by 3.25%?
questions.explain: To increase by 3.25% you keep the whole original (1) and add 0.0325, so multiply by 1.0325. Multiplying by 0.0325 alone gives only the increase, and 3.25% is 0.0325 — moving the decimal only one place gives 0.325, which is 32.5%.

questions.question: A dairy near Abbotsford shipped 250 kg of cheese last month. This month it ships 0.4% more than last month. What is this month's mass of cheese?
questions.explain: 0.4% is 0.004, so multiply 250 × 1.004 = 251 kg. Slipping the decimal point turns 0.4% into 4% (260 kg) or 40% (350 kg), and 1 kg is just the size of the increase.

questions.question: A school play sold 1 500 tickets last year. This year ticket sales increased by 120%. How many tickets were sold this year?
questions.explain: An increase of 120% means multiply by 1 + 1.20 = 2.2, so 1 500 × 2.2 = 3 300 tickets. The 1 800 is only the increase (1 500 × 1.2), and 120% is 1.2 as a decimal — not 0.012 or 12.

questions.question: A bag of trail mix has a mass of 900 g. The label warns the true mass may be 0.75% less than that. Which calculation gives the smallest mass the bag could have?
questions.explain: A 0.75% decrease keeps 100% − 0.75% = 99.25% of the mass, so multiply by 0.9925. Multiplying by 0.0075 gives only the mass lost, and shifting the decimal turns 0.75% into 7.5% (0.925) or 75% (0.25).

questions.question: An orchard in the Okanagan had 12 000 apple trees in 2024. During 2025 the number of trees increased by 150%. During 2026 the 2025 total then decreased by 0.5% because of frost. How many trees does the orchard have at the end of 2026?
questions.explain: First 12 000 × 2.5 = 30 000 trees, then 30 000 × 0.995 = 29 850 trees. The 18 000 is only the growth without the original orchard, and 0.5% is 0.005 — reading it as 5% takes off 1 500 trees instead of 150.

questions.question: A small BC town had a population of 6 400 in 2020. By 2023 the population had grown by 250%. From 2023 to 2024 the population then fell by 0.5%. What was the population in 2024?
questions.explain: Growing by 250% means multiplying by 3.5, so 6 400 × 3.5 = 22 400, and then 22 400 × 0.995 = 22 288 people. Multiplying by only 2.5 finds 250% of the town instead of the original plus 250% more.

questions.question: A season ski pass at a local hill costs $480, and club members get 12.5% off. Maya calculates 480 × 0.125 = 60 and says a member pays $60 for the pass. What is the mistake, and what does a member really pay?
options: Nothing is wrong; the $60 is the price she pays.
That $60 is the discount; she pays $420.
She should add 12.5%, so she pays $540.
questions.explain: 480 × 0.125 = 60 is the money taken off, so the price paid is 480 − 60 = $420, or in one step 480 × 0.875. Mixing up the discount with the sale price is the most common slip here.

questions.question: A Kelowna orchard sold 2 000 boxes of cherries last summer. This summer the number of boxes sold rose by 0.6%. Each box sells for $25. How much money did the orchard take in this summer?
questions.explain: Add the percent to 100% first: 100% + 0.6% = 100.6% = 1.006, so 2 000 × 1.006 = 2 012 boxes, and 2 012 × $25 = $50 300. The trap is stopping at the extra 12 boxes, worth only $300, which is the increase and not the new total.

questions.question: A hatchery near Chilliwack released 400 000 salmon fry in the spring. Over the summer the number of fry fell by 0.75%. In the fall, a new batch raised the summer number by 150%. How many fry does the hatchery have in the fall?
questions.explain: Work one step at a time: a 0.75% drop gives 400 000 × 0.9925 = 397 000, then a 150% rise gives 397 000 × 2.5 = 992 500. The usual trap is writing 0.75% as 0.075 — move the decimal point two places, so 0.75% = 0.0075.

questions.question: An art set at a Victoria bookstore costs $150. The store lowers the price by 0.8%. Noah works out 150 × 0.008 = 1.20 and says the new price of the art set is $1.20. What went wrong?
options: His method is fine — $1.20 is the sale price.
$1.20 is the drop; the new price is $148.80.
0.8% is 0.08, so the new price is $138.00.
The drop is added, so the price is $151.20.
questions.explain: A 0.8% drop leaves 99.2% of the price, so multiply the original amount: 150 × 0.992 = $148.80. The trap is answering 150 × 0.008 = $1.20, which is only the amount taken off, not the new price.

questions.question: A weather station near Prince George recorded 1 500 mm of snow last winter. This winter it expects 0.6% more snow than last winter. Liam multiplies 1 500 × 1.06 and writes 1 590 mm. What went wrong?
options: 0.6% is 0.06, so his 1 590 mm answer is right.
Only the rise counts, so the answer is 9 mm.
0.6% is 0.006, so the new total is 1 509 mm.
Take the 0.6% off instead, giving 1 491 mm.
questions.explain: Move the decimal point two places to change a percent to a decimal: 0.6% = 0.006, so the multiplier is 1.006 and 1 500 × 1.006 = 1 509 mm. Using 1.06 treats it as 6%, ten times too big.
